packs.title: Mission, Gardens and Coast
packs.promise: Explore Santa Barbara through separate mission, garden, coast and habitat outings.

q.s: Turn a collection into a field question.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official source route.
Choose one regional specimen, habitat or scientific theme from an open exhibition or official museum description.
Write a question about where or how that feature might appear outside; do not claim a current exhibit is open without checking.

q.s: Connect an open path with a protected cliff edge.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official source route.
From an open signed trail or city park map, find one bluff-view point and one safe return point.
Sketch the path and describe why staying back from the edge protects you and the habitat.

q.s: Choose a small urban garden comparison.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official source route.
On an open path or city garden page, choose one native or low-water planting and another garden feature.
Make a two-part sketch of how planting and public resting space fit together.

packs.title: Downtown to the Waterfront
packs.promise: Walk from Santa Barbara's civic and arts blocks to its working wharf and beach.

st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official source route.
At the open branch or in its official catalog, choose three different resource types for a Santa Barbara question.
Order the three checks and note which would establish a date, image or local place most directly.

q.s: Compare a family room with the public plaza.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official source route.
From a ticketed house visit or the Trust's official room descriptions, select one domestic or store feature.
Contrast its private family function with the adjacent public street or plaza.

q.s: Separate working structure from visitor shops.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official source route.
From an open public wharf approach or the city's official wharf page, identify one timber or working-waterfront feature.
Explain how it supports a wharf role beyond shopping or dining; no purchase or fishing is needed.
